intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer 2026, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Sample local cheeses, olives, honey, fresh seafood, and cured meats. Stop at a traditional taverna for a mezze spread including tzatziki, spanakopita, and grilled octopus paired with local ouzo or wine.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach on Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful coastal settings.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Santorini
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class where a local chef teaches you to prepare authentic Greek dishes such as moussaka, fresh tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes), fava dip, and baklava. Learn about local Santorinian ingredients like white eggplant and Assyrtiko wine, then enjoy the meal you've prepared.

experiences.name: Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Head to Myrtos Beach on Kefalonia, consistently ranked among Europe's best beaches. The dramatic white pebble shore contrasts with vivid turquoise water framed by steep green cliffs. Arrive in the late afternoon to swim and then watch the spectacular sunset paint the cliffs golden — a truly magical and nearly free experience.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Collect luggage, take the most affordable transfer option (public bus or shared shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort layout. Grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour kiosk or the resort's snack bar if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a local kiosk or convenience store near the resort — gyros wrap or tiropita (cheese pie) for under €3

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy levels low tonight — it's a late arrival. Confirm resort check-in details in advance since it's after 10 PM. Set an alarm to enjoy a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade directly accessible from Aegean Bliss Resort. Dip your toes in the warm Aegean Sea for the first time and scout the local beach scene. Pick up a Greek coffee (frappe) from a nearby café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the resort's beachfront. Swim in the warm sea (average 24–26°C in June), soak up the sun, and get comfortable with your surroundings. Walk to the nearest local village or beach strip to find a budget-friendly taverna for lunch. Explore the immediate neighborhood on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center for a casual evening walk (volta). Browse local shops and get a feel for the area. Find a traditional souvlaki or gyros stand for a budget dinner.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local bakery or supermarket — around €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or Greek salad at a beachside taverna — budget around €8–12
meals.dinner: Souvlaki pita wrap with tzatziki from a local grill house — €3–4 each

day_by_day.notes: Today is a gentle orientation day. Hydrate well — June temperatures average 29°C. Pick up a reusable water bottle and fill it at the resort to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim at the resort beach before the crowds arrive — the sea is calm and clear in the mornings. Then visit the nearest local open-air market (laiki agora) if one operates today. Browse fresh produce, olives, cheeses, and local honey. Great chance to stock up on cheap snacks for the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby hidden or less-touristy beach accessible by local bus or a short walk. Bring snacks from the morning market. Swim, snorkel if you brought gear, and relax. Look for sea urchins, octopus, and colorful fish in the clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and visit a local taverna for a traditional Greek dinner. Try moussaka or pastitsio — hearty, affordable, and authentically Greek.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach and feta pie) and a coffee from a local bakery — €2–3
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with market finds: olives, bread, feta, tomatoes — €5 total
meals.dinner: Moussaka or pastitsio with a glass of house wine at a local taverna — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules the night before for the nearby beach trip. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water for the afternoon beach session.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby archaeological site or ancient ruins — most Greek regions have accessible historical sites within a short bus or taxi ride. Explore at your own pace. Early morning is best before the heat peaks. Bring water and wear comfortable shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back toward the coast and find a shaded café or ouzeri (traditional Greek bar) for a long Greek lunch. Order mezedes (small shared dishes) — a budget-friendly and social way to eat. Try taramosalata, dolmades, and grilled halloumi.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the beach promenade. Find a spot on the rocks or beach to watch the sunset over the Aegean — completely free and spectacular. Grab a cheap beer or local wine from a mini-market and enjoy the view.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) and Greek coffee from a street vendor — €1.50
meals.lunch: Mezedes spread at an ouzeri — €10–14 per person including a drink
meals.dinner: Light dinner of grilled sardines and horiatiki (village salad) at a seaside taverna — €9–12

day_by_day.notes: Check entry fees for archaeological sites — many are free or reduced on certain days. EU students under 25 often get free entry. Sunset times in June are around 8:45–9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or ferry to a nearby island or coastal town for a day trip. Depart early to maximize time. Walk through the old town or port area, admire whitewashed buildings, and visit the local church or chapel for a cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a quieter beach on the day-trip destination — away from the main tourist beach. Swim and relax. Buy a fresh coconut or fruit juice from a beach vendor. Explore the local fishing harbor and watch fishermen bring in their catch.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry or bus before dark. Have dinner at the resort area — try a different taverna than previous nights. Order fresh catch-of-the-day fish, simply grilled with lemon and olive oil.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — toast with local honey and tea at the resort or a nearby café — €2–4
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus and fries at the day-trip destination's harbor taverna — €10–13
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh fish of the day with vegetables and bread at a local taverna — €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry or bus timetables the day before. Round-trip ferry tickets on local routes are typically €5–15. Bring cash as smaller island shops may not accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and beach morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Practice snorkeling or simply float in the warm sea. Read a book under an umbrella. This is a slower-paced recovery day after the day trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus ride to explore a different section of the local coastline. Look for a secluded cove or pebble beach. Bring a picnic lunch. Collect sea glass or shells as free souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Cook or self-cater dinner tonight to save money — visit a local supermarket and pick up ingredients for a simple Greek-style meal: bread, olives, feta, canned fish, and fresh vegetables. Eat at the resort or on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with fresh fruit from the supermarket — €2–3
meals.lunch: Picnic: bread, hummus, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, and local cheese — €4–5
meals.dinner: Self-catered supermarket meal: feta, olives, canned sardines, crusty bread, and a local beer — €6–8 total

day_by_day.notes: Self-catering one or two meals a week is one of the best ways to keep costs down on a budget trip to Greece. Local supermarkets (like Lidl or AB Vassilopoulos) have excellent affordable products.

day_by_day.morning: Mid-trip exploration day. Visit a local village inland — take a bus or shared taxi. Walk through narrow alleyways, visit the central plateia (village square), and chat with locals. Visit a small Orthodox church if open — they are usually free and beautifully decorated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a local kafeneion (traditional Greek coffee house) and order a Greek coffee. Watch locals play backgammon (tavli). This is a genuine cultural experience that costs almost nothing. Then browse any local craft or food shops for affordable souvenirs like local honey, olive oil, or herbs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast for dinner. Try a psarotaverna (fish tavern) — order grilled calamari or shrimp saganaki (shrimp in tomato and feta sauce) as a budget-friendly seafood option.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita or bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) from a village bakery — €2
meals.lunch: Village taverna set menu or daily special — typically €8–10 including bread and water
meals.dinner: Grilled calamari and shrimp saganaki at a psarotaverna — €11–14

day_by_day.notes: Inland villages are often cooler than the coast — a nice break from the beach heat. Buses to inland villages may be infrequent; check schedules carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day focused on water activities. Try paddleboarding or kayaking — many beaches offer affordable hourly rentals (€5–10/hour). Explore the coastline from the water for a new perspective. Early morning water is especially calm.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the beach to find a local beach bar or chiringuito for a long, lazy afternoon. Order a fresh lemonade or local beer. People-watch and relax. No agenda needed.
day_by_day.evening: Join a free or low-cost local event if available — check resort noticeboards or local tourism offices for live music, cultural performances, or open-air cinema events that often happen in summer.

meals.breakfast: Freddo espresso and a croissant or koulouri at a beachside café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Beach bar snack: club sandwich or Greek pita with tzatziki — €6–8
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek BBQ (souvlakia) at a local grill restaurant — mixed grill platter with pita and sides — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Paddle rental prices are negotiable if it's not peak busy time. Always agree on price before renting. Check the resort noticeboard for free evening events — many Greek coastal towns host summer festivals in June.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local food market or port in the morning to watch fishermen unload the night's catch. This is a vivid, authentic Greek experience. Buy fresh fruit or pastries from nearby stalls. Walk along the harbor and admire the colorful fishing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip — look for affordable group boat excursions that visit sea caves, blue lagoons, or nearby islets. These often cost €15–25 per person and include swimming stops. Book locally for the best prices rather than through hotel desks.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a harbor-front taverna — order whatever fresh fish was caught that morning. Ask the waiter what's fresh today (ti einai fresko simera?) for the best value and quality.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, a pastry, and Greek coffee from the port market — €3
meals.lunch: Light snack on the boat trip or packed lunch brought from the supermarket — €3–5
meals.dinner: Fresh catch of the day at a harbor taverna with local wine — €13–16

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip the day before directly with the operator at the port — you'll often get a better price than booking through tourist agencies. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast, and spend time journaling or reading by the sea. Take a gentle swim and enjoy the resort facilities. This is a recharge day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a different beach further along the coast — take a local bus or rent a bicycle (€8–12/day) for the afternoon. Discover a less-visited stretch of coastline. Bring snacks and plenty of water.
day_by_day.evening: Try cooking a meal together or solo using local ingredients — buy fresh vegetables, olive oil, and pasta from the supermarket and make a simple Greek-inspired pasta or salad. Eat on the balcony or beach.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a local café: eggs, tomatoes, feta, olives, and bread — €5–7
meals.lunch: Packed picnic on the bike ride: pita, tzatziki, and fresh fruit — €4
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with local olive oil, sun-dried tomatoes, and feta — €5–7 total

day_by_day.notes: Bicycle rental is a fantastic budget way to explore the coastline. Ask the resort or a local shop for the nearest rental point. Always wear sunscreen even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby monastery or hilltop chapel — these are often free and offer breathtaking panoramic views of the sea and landscape. Go early before the heat peaks. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the beach for a final full afternoon of swimming and sunbathing. Revisit your favorite spot from the trip. Take photos, collect memories, and soak in the Aegean atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner tonight — treat yourself to a proper sit-down meal at one of the better local tavernas. Order a full spread: starter, main, and dessert (try galaktoboureko — custard pastry, or loukoumades — honey doughnuts).

meals.breakfast: Homemade-style breakfast: supermarket yogurt, honey, granola, and fresh fruit — €3
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch: grilled corn from a beach vendor and fresh watermelon — €3–4
meals.dinner: Three-course splurge dinner at a quality local taverna — starter, grilled lamb chops or fresh fish, dessert, and wine — €20–25

day_by_day.notes: The monastery/chapel visit may require a short hike — wear sturdy sandals or sneakers. Bring a scarf or shawl to cover up at the entrance. The evening meal is your one planned splurge — enjoy it fully.

day_by_day.morning: Last full morning at the beach — take one final long swim in the warm Aegean. Collect any remaining souvenirs: local olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, or handmade ceramics from a local artisan shop. These make excellent affordable gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore any remaining local spots you haven't visited. Revisit a favorite café or taverna for a sentimental last lunch. Take a slow walk through the local town, sit in the main square, and absorb the atmosphere one more time.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset viewing from your favorite spot discovered during the trip. Then enjoy a farewell dinner at your favorite taverna from the week — a fitting end to the Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek bakery breakfast — fresh bougatsa and a freddo cappuccino — €4
meals.lunch: Revisit your favorite taverna for a sentimental last lunch — gyros, Greek salad, and local wine — €10–12
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your top taverna pick of the trip — order your favorite dishes from the week — €13–16

day_by_day.notes: Buy food souvenirs at local supermarkets or markets — they're much cheaper than tourist shops. Vacuum-sealed olives, honey, and dried oregano travel well. Begin packing tonight to avoid a rushed morning.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early, finish packing, and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take one last look at the Aegean Sea. Grab a quick breakfast nearby before heading to the airport. Allow plenty of time for the transfer — budget transport (public bus or shared shuttle) takes longer than private taxis.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport with ample time. Browse duty-free for any last-minute gifts (Greek olive oil, mastiha products, or local spirits like ouzo or tsipouro are great buys). Reflect on 13 wonderful days in Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece. Review your favorite memories, photos, and flavors from the trip. Start planning your next Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast near the resort or at the airport — coffee and a pastry — €3–5
meals.lunch: Airport meal or food brought from a local bakery before departure — €5–8
meals.dinner: On the plane or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 AM — confirm with the resort. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some euros for any last-minute transport or tips.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange pre-booked transfer or taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and unwind on the hotel terrace with a welcome drink.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel bar or a quick gyros wrap from a nearby 24-hour souvlaki stand en route from the airport.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival is late. Confirm transfer booking in advance and have hotel address in Greek script handy for the taxi driver. Exchange some euros at the airport for small expenses.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Afterwards, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to get your bearings, spot local cafés, and soak in the first views of the Aegean Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest main beach. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, swim in the warm Aegean waters, and simply decompress from travel. Explore the beach bar scene and try a local Mythos or Alfa beer with a light snack.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the nearest village or harbor area for your first proper Greek dinner. Watch the sunset over the water before heading back to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel buffet breakfast — enjoy Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, fresh fruit, and strong Greek coffee.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch — try a classic Greek salad (horiatiki), fresh calamari, and warm pita bread. Budget around €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Waterfront taverna dinner — order grilled sea bream (tsipoura), tzatziki, and a carafe of local house wine. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Apply high-SPF sunscreen from the start — the Greek summer sun is intense even in the morning. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby ancient archaeological site or hilltop viewpoint in the morning when it is cooler. Explore ruins or a Byzantine church and learn about the local history through informative plaques or a local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a midday swim and rest during peak heat hours (13:00–16:00). Optional: book a 60-minute traditional Greek massage at the hotel spa for a mid-range treat.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local market street or a pedestrian shopping lane. Pick up some local products — thyme honey, olive oil, or handmade ceramics — then settle into a mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) for a social, sharing-style dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — try a tiropita (cheese pie) or spanakopita (spinach pie) with a freddo espresso at a street café.
meals.lunch: Light poolside or hotel snack — a club sandwich or mezze platter to keep energy up without overeating in the heat.
meals.dinner: Mezedopoleio dinner — order a spread of dolmades, saganaki (fried cheese), gigantes plaki (giant beans), and grilled octopus. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the archaeological site visit. Many sites open early (08:00) and are best visited before 11:00 to avoid the heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day boat trip or water taxi to a nearby secluded cove or small islet. Snorkel in crystal-clear waters, explore hidden sea caves, and enjoy the unspoiled coastline away from the main tourist beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore by early afternoon. Rinse off and relax at the hotel pool. Read, nap, or enjoy a poolside cocktail during the hottest part of the day.
day_by_day.evening: Join a local cooking class or food experience if available nearby — learn to make moussaka, tzatziki, or baklava with a local host. Alternatively, visit a traditional psarotaverna (fish taverna) at the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the boat trip — pack a water bottle and light snacks for the excursion.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the boat — the tour operator often provides fresh fruit, local cheese, olives, and bread, or pack your own from a local deli.
meals.dinner: Cooking class includes a shared meal, or psarotaverna dinner — grilled whole fish of the day, shrimp saganaki, and local white wine (Assyrtiko). Budget €28–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip in advance, especially in June. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. Snorkeling gear is usually provided but confirm beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter, ATV, or car for the day and drive to a more distant, less-crowded beach on the other side of the island or coastline. Enjoy the scenic drive through olive groves, vineyards, and traditional villages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the secluded beach — swim, snorkel, and explore the natural surroundings. Visit a small seaside chapel or clifftop viewpoint along the way back.
day_by_day.evening: Return the vehicle and wind down with a sunset cocktail at a clifftop bar or rooftop lounge. Dine at a local taverna in a quieter neighborhood away from the main tourist strip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up before the day's driving.
meals.lunch: Roadside or village taverna lunch — try local specialties such as slow-cooked lamb, village sausages, or fresh-caught fish at a family-run spot. Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Neighborhood taverna dinner — roasted chicken with lemon and oregano (kotopoulo lemonato), horta (wild greens), and local red wine. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm you have a valid international driving permit if renting a car. Scooter rental is typically €20–30/day; car rental €40–60/day. Fill up on fuel before heading to remote areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local farmers' market or weekly street market (laiki agora) in the nearest town. Browse stalls selling fresh produce, spices, local cheeses, honey, and handmade goods. Chat with vendors and taste samples.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the beach for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing session. Try paddleboarding or kayaking — rentals are widely available at mid-range beach resorts.
day_by_day.evening: Take an evening walk through the old town or village quarter. Explore narrow alleyways, whitewashed houses with bougainvillea, and small Byzantine churches before settling in for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — pick up fresh bread, local honey, figs, and a wedge of graviera or feta cheese from the market stalls. Enjoy with a coffee at a nearby café.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — a grilled corn on the cob, loukoumades (honey doughnuts), or a fresh sandwich. Budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek taverna with live music — try pastitsio (Greek-style baked pasta), lamb chops (paidakia), and a glass of local retsina or Xinomavro wine. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Markets typically run Tuesday and Saturday mornings, starting around 07:30. Bring a reusable bag and small cash for purchases. Arrive early for the best selection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby island or significant coastal town via ferry or fast boat. Spend the morning exploring the main port, local architecture, and any notable landmarks or museums.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the island or town's best beach in the afternoon. Have a long, leisurely Greek lunch at a harbor-front restaurant before catching the return ferry.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner close to the hotel or at the hotel restaurant to rest after the day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing for the ferry.
meals.lunch: Harbor restaurant on the day-trip island — fresh lobster pasta (astakomakaronada) or shrimp risotto with a cold local beer. Budget €25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or nearby simple taverna — a lighter meal such as grilled vegetables, hummus, and pita with a glass of wine. Budget €18–24 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance and book tickets early in summer. Bring a light jacket for the return ferry ride as it can be breezy on the water in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning — sleep in, enjoy a slow hotel breakfast, and spend time reading or journaling on the balcony or beach. Optional: take an early morning swim before the beach gets busy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local winery or olive oil producer for a guided tasting tour. Learn about Greek wine varieties (Assyrtiko, Moschofilero, Agiorgitiko) and traditional olive oil production methods.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at one of the region's most scenic viewpoint restaurants. Book a table in advance for the best seats with panoramic Aegean views.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — try all the Greek specialties: loukoumades, taramosalata, fresh orange juice, and mountain tea.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the winery — cheese and charcuterie board, olives, and bread paired with wine tastings. Budget €15–20 per person including tastings.
meals.dinner: Scenic viewpoint restaurant — grilled branzino with capers and lemon, roasted potatoes, and a bottle of local white wine. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Winery tours typically cost €10–20 per person and should be booked ahead. Designate a non-drinking driver if renting a vehicle, or arrange a taxi for the winery visit.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike or nature walk along a scenic coastal trail or inland path. Many Greek islands and coastal regions have well-marked trails through pine forests, wildflower meadows, and along dramatic cliff edges with sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off with a long swim at a beach discovered on the hike or return to the hotel pool. Enjoy a siesta during peak afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Explore a different neighborhood or village for dinner. Look for a local psistaria (grill house) for an authentic, no-frills Greek grilling experience.

meals.breakfast: Early, energizing hotel breakfast before the hike — eggs, whole grain bread, fruit, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch for the trail — olives, cheese, bread, dried fruit, and water from a local minimarket. Budget €6–10.
meals.dinner: Psistaria grill house — mixed meat platter with lamb chops, chicken souvlaki, pork skewers, pita, and tzatziki. Budget €18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike before 09:00 to avoid the midday heat. Wear proper footwear, bring at least 1.5 liters of water per person, and apply sunscreen and insect repellent. Download an offline trail map (AllTrails) before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a traditional Greek monastery or historic church in the area. Many are set in stunning natural locations — on hilltops, cliffs, or nestled in valleys — and offer a peaceful, culturally rich experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Beach afternoon at a well-known organized beach with facilities. Try a water sport activity such as jet skiing, banana boat, or parasailing for a mid-afternoon adrenaline boost.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the harbor or marina for a pre-dinner ouzo or tsipouro at a traditional ouzeri with mezedes. Then walk to a nearby seafood restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — Greek coffee (ellinikos kafes) and a koulouri (sesame bread ring) from a street vendor.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna — grilled octopus, fresh bread, and a cold Alfa beer. Budget €15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Seafood restaurant at the harbor — mixed seafood platter, fish soup (kakavia), and local white wine. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting monasteries — shoulders and knees must be covered. Many monasteries are closed midday (13:00–17:00), so plan the morning visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided food tour of the local area if available — visit a local bakery, cheese shop, herb garden, and traditional kitchen to taste and learn about Greek culinary traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for personal exploration — revisit a favorite beach, do some souvenir shopping, or simply relax at the hotel pool with a book and a cocktail.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant for a special dinner — a mid-range fine dining Greek restaurant offering modern interpretations of traditional dishes with quality local ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Light café breakfast — freddo cappuccino and a bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) from a local zacharoplasteio (patisserie).
meals.lunch: Food tour includes tastings — you will sample enough to constitute a full lunch. Supplement with additional purchases from the bakery or cheese shop.
meals.dinner: Elevated Greek restaurant — beetroot salad with manouri cheese, slow-cooked lamb with orzo (giouvetsi), and a bottle of Santorini Assyrtiko. Budget €40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Food tours typically cost €45–70 per person and last 3–4 hours. Book well in advance as they fill up quickly in summer. Wear comfortable shoes as the tour involves a lot of walking.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — return to your favorite beach from the trip. Swim, float, and take in the Aegean one last time. Collect a few small stones or shells as a memento.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — pick up local honey, olive oil, herbs, ceramics, or evil eye (mati) charms for friends and family. Pack purchases carefully to protect fragile items.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best taverna you discovered during the trip. Order your favorite dishes from the week and toast to the trip with a glass of local wine or ouzo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite of Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit.
meals.lunch: Casual beach snack — a souvlaki wrap or fresh fruit from a beach vendor. Budget €6–10.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at your favorite taverna — revisit the best meal of the trip and order a round of loukoumades with honey and cinnamon for dessert. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening to avoid a stressful final morning. Leave out only what you need for the next day. Confirm your departure transfer or taxi booking for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last slow breakfast at the hotel. Take a short sunrise walk along the beach or hotel grounds to say goodbye to the Aegean. Check out of the hotel and arrange luggage storage if your flight is later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time: explore a final nearby attraction, café, or viewpoint near the airport area. Alternatively, relax in the hotel lobby or a nearby café with a final Greek coffee and pastry before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport, complete check-in and security, and depart Greece with wonderful memories, a full stomach, and a tan.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the last Greek coffee, honey, and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Airport café or a final souvlaki from a nearby takeaway before heading to departures. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for international departure. Keep snacks and a refillable water bottle in your carry-on. Declare any food items (honey, cheese) to customs if flying internationally. Kalo taxidi — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets. Sample local cheeses, olives, honey, fresh seafood, and cured meats. Stop at a traditional taverna for a mezze spread including tzatziki, spanakopita, and grilled octopus paired with local ouzo or wine.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach on Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small islet, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful coastal settings.

experiences.name: Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience
experiences.description: Head to Myrtos Beach on Kefalonia, consistently ranked among Europe's best beaches. The dramatic white pebble shore contrasts with vivid turquoise water framed by steep green cliffs. Arrive in the late afternoon to swim and then watch the spectacular sunset paint the cliffs golden — a truly magical and nearly free experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Athens International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. A private luxury transfer will be waiting to whisk you to the Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome drink and a light late-night amenity platter prepared by the resort's kitchen. Check in, settle into your beachfront suite, and rest.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome amenity platter in-suite: charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and fresh fruit provided by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with the resort concierge before travel. Request early check-in for luggage storage if arriving with hand baggage only. Keep Day 1 light — no excursions scheduled given the 22:30 landing.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start to your first full day. Take a slow morning walk along the resort's private beachfront as the sun rises over the Aegean. At 09:30, enjoy a lavish breakfast on the terrace overlooking the sea. Spend time acclimatizing — dip into the resort's infinity pool or take a gentle swim in the warm sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, embark on a guided orientation tour of the immediate coastal village. Stroll through whitewashed lanes, visit a local artisan shop, and browse a small seaside market for handcrafted goods and locally produced olive oil. Return to the resort by 17:00 for a sunset cocktail at the beach bar.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring modern Greek cuisine — think grilled octopus with fava purée, freshly caught sea bream, and a honey-and-walnut baklava dessert paired with a local Assyrtiko white wine.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast buffet at the resort terrace: fresh pastries, local honey, yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, eggs to order, cold cuts, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort's beach club: grilled halloumi salad, tzatziki with warm pita, and a chilled glass of rosé
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant tasting menu — modern Greek fine dining with wine pairing; budget approximately €120–€160 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle recovery day after travel. No major excursions planned. Use the day to rest, explore the immediate surroundings, and begin embracing the slow luxury pace of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private sunrise yoga session on the beach arranged by the resort (07:00–08:00). Follow with breakfast and then board a privately chartered speedboat at 10:00 for a morning coastal cruise. Explore hidden sea caves, secluded coves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters inaccessible by land. Snorkeling equipment provided on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anchor at a secluded private beach for a two-hour swim and sunbathing stop. The boat crew will serve a chilled seafood mezze lunch on deck — fresh shrimp, smoked salmon, calamari, and local dips. Return to the resort by 16:30 and unwind with a spa treatment — opt for a traditional Greek olive oil massage or a sea-salt body scrub at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a celebrated local taverna in the nearby fishing village for an authentic Greek dinner. Choose from the daily catch displayed on ice — whole grilled fish priced by weight — accompanied by village salad, grilled vegetables, and a carafe of local barrel wine. End the evening with a walk along the harbor promenade.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey and seasonal fruit, followed by eggs Benedict with smoked salmon at the resort terrace
meals.lunch: Seafood mezze on the private charter boat — calamari, grilled shrimp, smoked fish, tzatziki, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Upscale local fishing taverna: whole grilled sea bass or red mullet, village salad, grilled zucchini, and local wine; budget €70–€100 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the private speedboat charter through the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and a light cover-up. The spa should also be booked ahead to secure your preferred treatment time.

day_by_day.morning: Today features the Athens Central Market Food Tour. Depart the resort at 08:00 via private luxury vehicle to Athens (travel time varies by resort location — if resort is near Athens, approximately 1–2 hours). Arrive at Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) by 10:00. Join a premium guided food tour through the vibrant market halls: sample local cheeses, cured meats, fresh herbs, spices, olives, and street food. Visit surrounding specialty shops for honey, loukoumades (Greek donuts), and freshly ground coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, enjoy a leisurely lunch at a celebrated Athens restaurant near the Monastiraki or Psiri district. In the afternoon, take a private guided visit to the Acropolis and Parthenon (skip-the-line access). Admire panoramic views of Athens from the hilltop. Descend and explore the Acropolis Museum with a private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Athens with direct Acropolis views — an unforgettable setting for a premium Greek dining experience. Enjoy modern Greek cuisine: lamb chops with herb crust, grilled vegetable medley, and loukoumades with ice cream for dessert. Private transfer returns you to the resort afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort before departure: Greek pastries, coffee, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Acclaimed Athens taverna near Monastiraki: slow-cooked lamb kleftiko, spanakopita, and a glass of Nemea red wine; budget €50–€80 per person
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine-dining restaurant with Acropolis views: modern Greek tasting menu with wine pairing; budget €130–€180 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion to Athens. Pre-book skip-the-line Acropolis tickets and the private guide well in advance — summer queues can be very long. The food tour should also be reserved ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed morning at the resort. After breakfast, participate in a private Greek cooking class hosted by the resort's executive chef (09:30–12:30). Learn to prepare three traditional dishes: spanakopita, moussaka, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). Use fresh, locally sourced ingredients and enjoy your creations as lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at leisure on the resort's private beach. The sea temperature is warm and ideal for swimming. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from the beach club and explore the coastline at your own pace. Alternatively, relax on a sun lounger with a chilled drink from the beach bar and a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private sunset dinner on the beach — a bespoke experience arranged by the resort. A candlelit table is set on the sand with a personalized menu, dedicated butler service, and a curated wine list. Watch the sun dip below the horizon over the Aegean as you dine.

meals.breakfast: À la carte resort breakfast: freshly baked tiropita (cheese pie), Greek coffee, seasonal fruit platter, and avocado toast with feta
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class: homemade spanakopita, moussaka, and a Greek salad with fresh pita
meals.dinner: Private beach candlelit dinner arranged by the resort: personalized 4-course menu with wine pairing; budget €200–€250 per person (premium experience)

day_by_day.notes: The private beach dinner must be booked through the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance. This is a highlight experience — ideal for a special occasion or simply an indulgent evening. Bring a light wrap as sea breezes can be refreshing after sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the resort early (07:30) for a day trip to explore a nearby traditional Greek village in the hills. Hire a private driver and guide. Visit the village square, a centuries-old Orthodox church, and a family-run olive grove where you'll receive a private tour and tasting of extra-virgin olive oil and local olives. Purchase artisan products directly from the producers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a scenic hilltop viewpoint for panoramic coastal views. Enjoy a leisurely lunch at a family taverna in the village — one of those hidden gems known only to locals — serving slow-cooked stews, roasted meats, and homemade bread baked in a wood-fired oven. Return to the resort by 17:00 and enjoy an early evening swim.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a sophisticated seafood restaurant on the resort's waterfront strip. Opt for a seafood platter for two: lobster, langoustines, grilled octopus, and sea urchin, paired with a bottle of chilled Santorinian Assyrtiko. Finish with a digestif of local tsipouro (Greek grappa) at the bar.

meals.breakfast: Quick resort breakfast before departure: Greek yogurt, honey, nuts, and espresso
meals.lunch: Traditional village taverna: slow-cooked goat stew, roasted potatoes, village salad, homemade bread, and local wine; budget €35–€55 per person
meals.dinner: Upscale waterfront seafood restaurant: premium seafood platter with wine; budget €150–€200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Ask the concierge to arrange a reputable local driver-guide who speaks English and has deep knowledge of the region. Bring cash for village artisan purchases as many small producers don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Today features the Myrtos Beach Sunset Experience on Kefalonia. Arrange a private charter flight or high-speed ferry to Kefalonia (coordinate with the resort concierge based on your resort's exact location). Arrive on Kefalonia by mid-morning. Check into a luxury day suite at a boutique hotel near Myrtos for freshening up. Spend the morning exploring Assos village — a stunning peninsula village with a Venetian castle — and strolling its picturesque harbor.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, head to Myrtos Beach — consistently ranked among Europe's most dramatic and beautiful beaches. The sheer white limestone cliffs plunge dramatically to turquoise waters below. Descend to the beach for swimming and sunbathing on the white pebbles. The water is a vivid, almost unreal shade of blue-green. Stay through the golden hour for the legendary Myrtos sunset experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to a Kefalonia hilltop restaurant for dinner overlooking the island's coastline as dusk settles. Savor locally caught fish, Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), and Robola wine — the island's prized white variety. Return to the resort via private transfer or charter.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure: continental spread with pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Seaside restaurant near Assos village: grilled fish of the day, Greek salad, and a glass of Robola white wine; budget €60–€80 per person
meals.dinner: Kefalonia hilltop fine-dining restaurant: local specialties with Robola wine pairing; budget €90–€130 per person

day_by_day.notes: Myrtos Beach has limited shade and the pebbles can be hot underfoot — bring water shoes, a beach umbrella if possible, and plenty of water. The descent road to Myrtos is steep and winding; a 4x4 or confident local driver is recommended. Book all transport well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: A full rest and resort day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast on your private balcony overlooking the Aegean. Book a 90-minute couples' or solo spa journey at the resort spa: begin with a hammam steam ritual, followed by a full-body Greek honey and olive oil wrap, and conclude with a deep-tissue massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the spa, enjoy a light poolside lunch. Spend the afternoon reading, swimming, or simply soaking in the luxury of your beachfront setting. At 16:00, join an optional resort-hosted wine tasting session: a sommelier guides you through five premium Greek wines — from Assyrtiko to Xinomavro — paired with artisan cheeses and charcuterie.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a nearby acclaimed restaurant known for its creative Mediterranean cuisine. The chef blends Greek tradition with contemporary technique — expect dishes like slow-braised lamb with pomegranate reduction, saffron-scented seafood risotto, and pistachio-and-rose water panna cotta.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast on the private balcony: fresh pastries, Greek coffee, fruit, smoked salmon, and eggs to order — delivered by butler
meals.lunch: Poolside light lunch: grilled vegetable antipasto, burrata with heirloom tomatoes, and a chilled glass of rosé
meals.dinner: Creative Mediterranean fine-dining restaurant nearby: chef's tasting menu with wine pairing; budget €140–€180 per person

day_by_day.notes: The in-suite breakfast must be pre-ordered the evening before through the butler service. The wine tasting session may need advance registration at the resort's activities desk. A perfect day to recharge before the upcoming Zakynthos and Crete excursions.

day_by_day.morning: Today features the iconic Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) experience on Zakynthos. Depart early via private charter flight or high-speed ferry to Zakynthos (Zante). Arrive by 09:30. Board a privately chartered luxury boat at the marina for a morning coastal cruise around Zakynthos. Visit the famous Blue Caves — sea caves with luminescent blue water — before heading toward Navagio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) — accessible only by boat. Step onto the iconic white pebble beach surrounded by towering limestone cliffs and the rusted shipwreck of the MV Panagiotis. Swim in the impossibly clear turquoise water, explore the shipwreck up close, and soak in one of the most photographed settings in all of Greece. The private charter ensures you arrive before or after the main tourist rush for a more exclusive experience. Enjoy a chilled champagne and mezze spread on the boat.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Zakynthos town for a sunset dinner at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the Ionian Sea. Savor grilled lobster, fresh catch of the day, and local Zakynthian wines. Return to your resort via private transfer.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort: Greek pastries, coffee, and yogurt before departure
meals.lunch: On-board private charter spread: champagne, mezze platter (olives, dips, cheeses, cold cuts), fresh fruit, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Zakynthos rooftop fine-dining restaurant: grilled lobster, fresh fish, and local wine; budget €130–€170 per person

day_by_day.notes: Navagio Beach is only accessible by sea — there is no land route. Book a private luxury boat charter rather than a group tour for a more exclusive experience. Bring waterproof sandals as the beach is pebbled. Arrive early or late afternoon to avoid the midday crowd rush. Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect the marine environment.

day_by_day.morning: A relaxed morning at the resort following yesterday's full-day excursion. Enjoy a late breakfast, then take a guided snorkeling or scuba diving session organized by the resort's water sports center. The warm June sea (approximately 24–26°C) is ideal for underwater exploration. Discover colorful marine life, sea grass meadows, and rocky reef formations just off the resort's beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a light poolside lunch, embark on a private guided tour of a local archaeological site or Byzantine monument near the resort. Gain insight into the layers of Greek history — from ancient ruins to Venetian fortresses — with a knowledgeable private guide. Return to the resort by 17:30 for a sunset swim.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's casual-chic beach club restaurant. Dine barefoot in the sand with your feet practically in the sea. Order grilled whole fish, fresh salads, and end with loukoumades drizzled with thyme honey and cinnamon. Pair with a crisp local white wine.

meals.breakfast: Late resort breakfast: shakshuka with feta, fresh bread, Greek coffee, and a fruit platter
meals.lunch: Poolside mezze: hummus, grilled pita, stuffed vine leaves, grilled shrimp skewers, and sparkling water or rosé
meals.dinner: Resort beach club restaurant: grilled sea bream, fresh salad, and loukoumades dessert; budget €70–€100 per person

day_by_day.notes: The diving or snorkeling session should be booked through the resort's water sports desk. If certified, a guided scuba dive is highly recommended. The evening beach club dinner is a more casual experience — ideal after several high-energy excursion days.

day_by_day.morning: Today features the Elafonissi Beach Day Trip on Crete. Depart early via private charter flight or high-speed ferry to Crete. Arrive and transfer directly to Elafonissi Beach on the southwestern tip of Crete. The beach is world-famous for its pink-tinged sand — created by crushed coral and shells — and its shallow, warm lagoon-like waters. Arrive early (before 10:00) to enjoy the beach before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming, wading in the shallow pink lagoon, and exploring the small islet of Elafonissi (accessible on foot through the shallow water). The water is calm and crystal-clear — perfect for snorkeling. Enjoy a packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the resort or a local Cretan restaurant: fresh bread, local cheeses, cured meats, olives, and chilled wine. In the late afternoon, visit a nearby Cretan winery for a private tasting of Cretan wines and raki.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Cretan restaurant in Chania's Old Town — one of Greece's most beautiful medieval harbor towns. Dine on authentic Cretan cuisine: dakos (barley rusk salad), slow-braised lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and Cretan graviera cheese. Stroll the Venetian harbor after dinner before returning to the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure: continental spread, Greek coffee, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Premium packed picnic at Elafonissi: artisan bread, Cretan cheeses, cured meats, olives, fruit, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Acclaimed Cretan restaurant in Chania Old Town: traditional Cretan tasting menu with local wine and raki; budget €90–€130 per person

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a protected nature reserve — only reef-safe sunscreen is permitted and no umbrellas with stakes. The beach can get crowded by midday in summer, so arriving early is essential. Chania Old Town is a beautiful evening destination — allow time to wander the Venetian harbor and alleyways after dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Penultimate day — a special, indulgent morning. Pre-arrange a private sunrise boat excursion departing at 06:00 to watch the sun rise over the Aegean from the sea. Return by 08:30 for a champagne breakfast on the resort terrace. Spend the rest of the morning at leisure: final swim in the sea, last visit to the resort spa for a facial or foot treatment, and relaxed packing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a private guided olive oil and local produce tasting experience at a nearby estate. Learn about the ancient tradition of Greek olive cultivation, taste multiple varieties of extra-virgin olive oil, local honey, and artisan products. Purchase premium gifts and souvenirs to take home. Return to the resort by 16:00 for a final sunset swim.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final full evening in Greece with a grand dinner at the most prestigious restaurant in the area — either a Michelin-recognized venue or the resort's flagship fine-dining restaurant. Order the full chef's tasting menu with premium wine pairing. Toast to an extraordinary trip with a glass of aged Metaxa or a local dessert wine. Reflect on 13 days of sun, sea, and extraordinary Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the resort terrace after sunrise boat excursion: smoked salmon, eggs royale, fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, and Champagne
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch: Greek salad with premium Kalamata olives and feta, grilled octopus, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's flagship or top local fine-dining restaurant: full tasting menu with premium wine pairing and dessert; budget €180–€250 per person

day_by_day.notes: The farewell dinner reservation should be made at the start of the trip to secure the best table — ideally with a sea view. Consider ordering a special dessert or cake if celebrating a milestone. Ask the sommelier to recommend a bottle of aged Greek wine as a memorable final pairing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece. Enjoy one last slow breakfast at the resort — savor every bite knowing this is your farewell meal. Take a final walk along the private beach, collect a handful of sea glass or smooth pebbles as a keepsake, and take in the view of the Aegean one last time. Check out of the Aegean Bliss Resort at the agreed late check-out time (request 13:00 or 14:00 check-out through concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, the resort concierge will arrange a private luxury transfer to the airport. If time allows before the transfer, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café in the nearest village. At the airport, access the premium lounge for a comfortable pre-flight experience.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Greece with extraordinary memories of 13 days of luxury beaches, world-class cuisine, and Aegean splendor. The private transfer ensures a seamless, stress-free journey to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: full Greek spread — yogurt, honey, pastries, eggs to order, fresh juice, and Greek coffee enjoyed at a leisurely pace
meals.lunch: Light airport lounge snacks or a farewell coffee and pastry at a local village café before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport restaurant depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Request late check-out (13:00–14:00) from the resort concierge at least 48 hours in advance — this is typically complimentary or discounted for premium guests. Ensure all artisan purchases, olive oil, and wine bought throughout the trip are properly packed (liquids in checked luggage). Keep a small memento — a sea pebble, a jar of local honey, or a bottle of Assyrtiko — as a lasting reminder of Greece.
